correctness.rationale: Two edges that meet are compatible by bipartiteness. A disjoint pair is compatible exactly when both cross-edges were deleted, which forces a unique reciprocal partner; a third edge would have to meet both and be one of the missing cross-edges. A pairwise-intersecting family lies in one star because there are no triangles. This partitions packings into empty, singletons, unique-center star subsets of size at least two, and reciprocal pairs. Every degree is at least two, so singletons extend, whole stars cannot extend, and the maximal polynomial follows. At saturation all vertices on the smaller shore lose one edge, while the other shore has degree at most the smaller shore size; the largest star has size max(m,n)-1, also when m=n. Below saturation the largest full-degree star survives. For topology, the nonempty intersection of any two star simplices is exactly the vertex for their shared graph edge; all higher intersections are empty. The good-cover nerve is thus G, connected because any two vertices of either shore share a neighbour, and it has cycle rank mn-t-m-n+1. Each reciprocal pair contributes one independent new interval attaching its two endpoints to the connected star complex; its attaching map from S^0 is homotopic to a constant, adding a circle. There are no additional higher faces. This proves actual homotopy equivalence, not just the recorded mod-two checks. It gives the stated Betti change t-2 and the maximal-size gap for balanced shores.
residual_risks: The finite log counts and mod-two homology checks do not establish the all-parameter result or the integral homotopy claim; those rest on the reviewed classification and nerve and attachment arguments.

Prior complete-biclique maximum and comparison with the distinct dissociation complexity
value.rationale: Matching deletion is the basic perturbation connecting complete bicliques to crown graphs. The reciprocal pair is a precise new type of maximal face, gives an unbounded gap in balanced maximal-size spectra, and accounts for every new circle relative to the star subcomplex. This is a single structural description of enumerative and integral topological behavior, not a table of small examples.
residual_risks: The scope is matching deletions with both shores of size at least three; no analogous result for arbitrary deletion patterns or equivariant homotopy is implied.
